data.title: Role of AMP-activated protein kinase in mechanism of metformin action

data.finding: Metformin activates AMPK, suppressing hepatic gluconeogenesis and lipogenesis.
data.abstract_excerpt: Metformin is a widely used drug for treatment of type 2 diabetes with no defined cellular mechanism of action. Its glucose-lowering effect results from decreased hepatic glucose production and increased glucose utilization. Metformin's beneficial effects on circulating lipids have been linked to reduced fatty liver. AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) is a major cellular regulator of lipid and glucose metabolism.

extracted_findings.effect: Metformin activates AMPK, explaining its glucose- and lipid-lowering effects
